_comment: What each fixture is for, and — for the invalid ones — which constraint must reject it.
Asserting merely that an invalid fixture is rejected is a weak test: a fixture that
becomes invalid for an unrelated reason (a typo, a renamed field) would still pass
while the constraint it was written to protect quietly stopped working. Naming the
expected path and keyword makes the test verify what it claims to verify.
'path' is the JSON pointer to the offending value; 'keyword' is the JSON Schema
keyword that must produce the failure.

valid.valid-jellyfin.json: The realistic case: large image, user-selected media storage, optional GPU, declared credentials, Stage 2 capabilities and structured events.
valid.valid-minimal.json: The smallest manifest the schema accepts. Guards against required fields being added carelessly — every addition here is a breaking change for every existing manifest.

invalid-privileged-container.json.why: Requests a privileged container. The schema pins permissions.privileged to const false, because a privileged container is a root shell on the host and no catalogue application will be granted one. If this fixture ever validates, that guarantee has been removed.

invalid-floating-tag.json.why: Pins the image to 'latest'. An application that silently changes version underneath a user is an application that silently breaks, and the user has no way to know why.

invalid-absolute-host-path.json.why: Tries to choose its own location on the host filesystem. Applications declare storage by role; Homebase decides where it lives. Allowing a host path would let a manifest escape /srv/homebase/.

invalid-missing-health.json.why: No health block. An application that cannot be checked cannot be managed — an unhealthy application reporting nothing is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

invalid-bad-capability-risk.json.why: Declares a Stage 2 capability with an invented risk level. Risk levels are what the policy engine decides on, so an unrecognised value must never be silently accepted as safe.

valid.valid-recoverable.json: A recoverable error carrying the recovery instruction it is required to have.
valid.valid-unrecoverable.json: An unrecoverable error, which needs no recovery instruction.

invalid-recoverable-without-recovery.jso.why: Claims to be recoverable but does not say how. Telling a user their problem is fixable while withholding the fix is worse than saying nothing.

invalid-code-format.json.why: Error code is not lowercase domain.reason. Codes are the machine-readable contract clients switch on; an inconsistent one is a code nobody can match against reliably.
